# 02 Resolve a parsed document into a validated graph model

## Outcome

`buildGraphModel(document)` turns a `SirenDocument` into a normalized `GraphModel`: every edge
gets a stable id, every `timeline:` reference is resolved against real node/edge ids (or flagged
as a diagnostic and dropped rather than failing the whole graph), and elements are grouped by the
step that reveals them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given a `SirenDocument` fixture with nodes `A`, `B`, `C` and edges `A->B`, `B->C`,
  `buildGraphModel` assigns edge ids `A-B` and `B-C`.
- [ ] A second edge between the same pair (`A->B` declared twice) gets ids `A-B` and `A-B#2`.
- [ ] Given a `timeline:` with `step 1: enter B fade` and `step 2: enter C fade, enter A-B fade`,
  the resulting `ResolvedTimeline` groups `{1: [B], 2: [C, A-B]}`, and `graph.nodes`/`graph.edges`
  correctly mark which elements start pending (anything appearing in the timeline at step > 0)
  vs. immediately visible (`A`, never mentioned).
- [ ] A `timeline:` entry referencing an id that doesn't exist in the document produces an
  error-severity diagnostic; that single entry is dropped and the rest of the graph still builds
  (`graph` is not `null`).
- [ ] A document with two nodes sharing the same id but different bracket labels produces a
  warning diagnostic; `buildGraphModel` keeps the first-seen label.
- [ ] A document with no `timeline:` block at all produces a `GraphModel` whose
  `resolvedTimeline.totalSteps === 0` and every node/edge marked immediately visible.

## Test seam

`buildGraphModel(document: SirenDocument): { graph: GraphModel | null; diagnostics: Diagnostic[] }`
— unit level, pure function, hand-built `SirenDocument` fixtures (does not need the real parser).
